fact: ICT Minister Mavetera said the government introduced infrastructure sharing and mandated tower relocation using the Universal Service Fund as interventions to bridge the digital divide for underserved rural and remote communities, and wants the fund to yield 100% coverage of marginalised wards.
ICT Minister Mavetera said at Digital UNGA that more than 10,000 remote sites have been connected under Zimbabwe's digital inclusion initiatives.
The report says free Wi-Fi has been rolled out at rural business hubs under the Presidential Internet Scheme, and Community Information Centres modernised into Digital Centres.
MISA Zimbabwe states the Universal Service Fund finances network expansion into economically disadvantaged areas.

Minister Mavetera directed POTRAZ to set explicit Universal Service Fund targets for connectivity in schools, clinics, chiefs' courts, rural business centres and underserved communities, and to publish coverage, quality, affordability and uptake KPIs quarterly.
